subject: Alignment: DPA and cross-border risk mitigations
messages:
From: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@novatech.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novatech.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Alignment on DPA and cross-border risk mitigations

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciate the quick walkthrough of Redwood's hosting options. Legal has a couple of items they want tracked in the DPA and the transfer-impact write-up before procurement can move to signature. Key asks from NovaTech legal:
- Confirm processor/processor-subprocessor mapping and evidence for EU routing (we run EU users and need clarity on where KV caches and logs may be stored).
- A binding fallback plan when a primary EU model endpoint is unavailable (we need an orderly degradation to ensure user data stays in-region where possible).
- A short transfer-impact addendum that states the safeguards for cross-border requests and references the SCCs.

I've attached our template DPA redline and a one-page transfer-impact summary they expect. Can Redwood take a look and propose language or call out where you need exceptions? Procurement asked me to loop in the legal/ops folks on your side.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Stevens
Head of Legal Operations | NovaTech
emma.stevens@novatech.com
Attachment: NovaTech_DPA_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@novatech.com>
Cc: procurement@novatech.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on DPA and cross-border risk mitigations

Emma — thanks for sending this over and for the summary. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (Customer Success/Order Forms) to coordinate. I've scanned the redline and noted a few high-level items we should discuss:

1) Processor map & caches: our runtime can be configured to keep KV caching and logs in-region for EU-only customers on Dedicated or Private. For hosted accounts we can enforce EU-region routing and an access-control policy; we will call out the operational measures and the technical controls (KMS, retention windows).
2) Fallback behavior: we support policy-based routing with fallback to nearest compatible model. For NovaTech's risk profile we can add a clause committing to default EU-region fallback where capacity allows, plus an outage notification SLA and a migration plan for a holdover model with stricter data residency settings.
3) SCCs and TIA: we can accept the standard SCCs template but propose to append a short transfer-impact addendum describing technical and organizational safeguards.

Action items for us: Karthik to propose redline language on sections 3 (Data Transfers) and 5 (Subprocessors). Monica to confirm order form language and any billing impacts of Dedicated routing. Emma — can you confirm whether NovaTech needs explicit contractual guarantees for cache residency or whether operational statements + audit logs are sufficient?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@novatech.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on DPA and cross-border risk mitigations

Emma/Aditya — thanks. I reviewed the NovaTech redline and sketched specific contract language we can offer. High level: we can accept the SCCs, but need to limit liability carve-outs and clarify subprocessors notice windows. I attached a draft redline where I've: 
- Narrowed the cache/residency commitment to configuration available for Hosted EU-region accounts and Dedicated customers, with an operational evidence clause (monthly log extracts and a one-off attestation).
- Proposed a 30-day notice for adding major subprocessors, 7-day notice for urgent security-critical additions.
- Added fallback procedure language: in a rare cross-border failover (primary EU capacity exhausted), Redwood will (a) attempt EU-region alternatives, (b) if unavailable, fail over to a quantized in-region model variant where possible, and (c) notify NovaTech within 60 minutes and provide remediation steps.

Please review the attached redline (NovaTech_DPA_redline.docx) and the short transfer-impact addendum (transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf). Two questions for NovaTech:
1) Is a monthly log extract and annual attestation sufficient evidence for you?
2) Do you require the fallback model to be identical in capability (we can promise data residency but not 1:1 performance parity in every failover scenario)?

If both are okay we can move these edits to the Order Form (billing for Dedicated routing) and prep for signature.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf
Attachment: NovaTech_DPA_redline.docx

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@novatech.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on DPA and cross-border risk mitigations

Quick notes from order-form perspective:
- Dedicated routing (EU-only) will require a minor pricing delta on the Order Form; I attached an updated OrderForm-v2-redlines.xlsx with line-item placeholders.
- We should include a sentence in the Order Form that references the DPA annex for data-residency configuration and the SLA for outage notification. Keeps the DPA as the source of truth for the controls while the Order Form handles commercial terms.
- Jordan can own the operational runbook tie-out for onboarding (he's copied).

Emma — if you confirm the commercial delta is acceptable we can include the pricing footnote and push this to procurement for DocuSign.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: OrderForm-v2-redlines.xlsx

From: Emma Stevens <emma.stevens@novatech.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novatech-legal.io>, procurement@novatech.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 17:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on DPA and cross-border risk mitigations

Monica/Karthik/Aditya — this is helpful, thanks. A few quick answers:
- Evidence: monthly log extract + an annual attestation is acceptable for our risk team. We will reserve the right to request a one-off deeper audit (with reasonable notice) if we see anomalous activity.
- Fallback: NovaTech legal accepts the fallback language you proposed as long as it is coupled with the notification SLA and an explicit statement that we can pause cross-border routing during an incident.
- Commercial delta: procurement is ok with a modest line-item for Dedicated routing; please provide the exact TBD number and we'll include it in the PO.

Next steps — Karthik, can you consolidate the redline and the transfer-impact addendum into a single DPA draft? Monica, if you can add the pricing cell we will circulate the final Order Form to procurement and Olivia (cc'd). I'll ask Oliver to keep an eye on final legal signoff.

Best,
Emma
Emma Stevens
Head of Legal Operations | NovaTech
Attachment: none
